title: Freya and the Salt
premise: Coral Nakamura, a mercenary bound by an old oath to a god who has been silent for twenty years, makes their living guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers, Coral's own god wakes — and demands payment for its long silence: the soul of a child sold decades ago to the court beneath the mountain, where the last dragon-fire is guttering out and the underworld's rulers mean to extinguish it forever. Coral, along with a disgraced priestess named Sable and a runaway noble boy who can hear the mountain dreaming, must steal the soul back before the final flame dies — even though Coral's oath requires them to deliver it instead. In the end, Coral breaks their vow, offers their own name in place of the child's, and discovers that love freely given is the only offering the old gods ever truly wanted; the dragon-fire rekindles on that truth, and Coral walks out of the mountain belonging to no god at all — only to the family they made on the road.
about_author: Wren Kavanagh is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons in the northern ranges and now writes fantasy from a cabin full of unreliable maps. Their work explores oaths, exile, and the families we build when the ones we were given fall through.

chapters.title: The Silent Tithe
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral leads a smuggler caravan through Thornfell's high passes, paying ritual tribute at shrines to a god that never answers anymore. A young client, Tam, asks why they bother; Coral deflects. The emotional beat is weary habit masking grief — Coral still prays, and hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: Smoke from a Cold Altar
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a ruined shrine, Coral's offering ignites without kindling. A voice — their god, Vess — speaks for the first time in twenty years: a debt is called due. Coral flees into the storm, shaken, and the chapter ends with the mountains themselves seeming to lean in and listen.

chapters.title: The Priestess Who Drowned Her God
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the river town of Lowmark, defrocked priestess Sable recognizes Coral as the mercenary her order once hired to hunt her. Instead of turning them in, she begs passage: she heard prayers being answered too, and one of them was hers. Uneasy alliance forms; beat: two people united by shame.

chapters.title: What the Boy Heard Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral takes a job escorting Lord Aldric's runaway son, Perrin, who claims he hears the mountain 'dreaming' beneath Thornfell — voices counting down. When Perrin recites Coral's secret childhood prayer word-for-word, Coral realizes the boy is a conduit. Beat: fear curdling into reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: Tolls on the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Bandits loyal to the mountain court ambush the party; Coral's knowledge of hidden ways saves them, but the bandits' leader delivers a message: the court knows about the debt, and wants Coral to collect the soul for them. Beat: Coral learns they are already a piece on someone's board.

chapters.title: Vess Speaks in Three Tongues
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vess manifests through Sable's old rites, revealing the terms: the soul of a child sold to the undercourt forty years ago must be delivered before the last dragon-fire gutters out — or every answered prayer becomes a leash. Sable hides that the sold child was her brother. Beat: guilt sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The party shelters in a salt-mining village where the dead walk gently, tending hearths. Perrin bonds with the ghost-keepers; Coral sees found family working and aches. The ghosts warn: the undercourt buys souls with kindness first, cruelty after. Beat: tenderness foreshadowing horror.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath Sends an Invitation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An envoy of the undercourt arrives wearing Sable's mother's face, offering safe passage and a bargain: deliver the soul, and Sable's brother goes free. Sable nearly accepts. Coral refuses for both of them. Beat: the seduction of a deal that costs everything but promises home.

chapters.title: Descent at the Weeping Gate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The party enters the mountain through a gate that cries brine instead of water. Coral's smuggler instincts fail underground — here, roads move. Only Perrin can navigate by the mountain's dreams. Beat: competence inverted; Coral must learn to follow.

chapters.title: Markets Where Names Are Currency
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the undercourt's bazaar, memories and names are traded like spice. To buy information, Coral pawns a cherished memory of their mother; Sable watches them come back lighter and wrong. Beat: the cost of the quest begins to be paid in selfhood.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Guided by Perrin, they reach the vault where the last dragon-fire burns in a bowl of bone, and find the stolen soul kept beside it — a small, flickering light that calls Perrin 'brother.' Guards close in. Beat: wonder and dread entwined as the stakes become visible and finite.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bone Halls
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Perrin, terrified and tempted by the court's offer to make his nightmares stop, unlocks the gate for the guards. He immediately regrets it as Coral is captured shielding him. Beat: a child's weakness, forgiveness withheld, and the wound that will define his arc.

chapters.title: Chains of Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Imprisoned, Coral learns the court's truth: gods answer prayers to bind mortals, and Vess's 'debt' was always a trap to reclaim the fire's keeper-soul. Coral's lifelong devotion curdles. Beat: faith broken open — the novel's thematic hinge.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable trades her priesthood's last relic — her brother's death-mask — for Coral's release, confessing the sold soul is her nephew, the child her brother fathered before dying. Beat: sacrifice as penance; the found family tightens around shared loss.

chapters.title: The Long Way Through the Mountain's Dream
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Fleeing through shifting dream-passage, Perrin must face the mountain directly and apologize to it for his betrayal. The dream forgives him conditionally: he may lead, but every wrong turn will cost him a memory of home. Beat: redemption priced honestly.

chapters.title: Vess Unmasked
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vess corners the fugitives, dropping all pretense: it will consume the soul and the last flame together to become the only god left. Coral formally renounces their oath — and the world holds its breath to see if a mortal can survive unbinding. Beat: defiance as identity.

chapters.title: What Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the flame's vault, the dying dragon-fire shows each of them a memory: Coral's mother singing, Sable's brother laughing, Perrin's first snow. The fire does not want worship; it wants witness. Beat: revelation that love, not duty, fuels the divine.

chapters.title: The Offering of a Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax begins: as Vess descends to devour the flame, Coral offers not the child's soul but their own name — freely given, the one currency the court cannot counterfeit. The bargain hangs unresolved as Vess hesitates between hunger and something older. Beat: ultimate risk, cliff-edge tension.

chapters.title: Ashes Vote No
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Climax resolves: the mountain itself — every ghost, every salt-dead villager, every remembered prayer — rises against Vess. Perrin leads the dead; Sable unmakes the false bargain with her relic; the soul-child is freed into the flame. Beat: collective salvation, found family as army.

chapters.title: Rekindling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The dragon-fire blazes back to life on Coral's offered name, burning away Vess's claim rather than Coral's self — the gods accept love, not ownership. The undercourt crumbles; the survivors climb toward daylight carrying the child, now breathing and warm. Beat: catharsis after sacrifice.

chapters.title: Belonging to No One
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Above ground, the three reckon with what remains: Sable buries her brother's mask at last; Perrin chooses to stay with them over his father's house; Coral, nameless to gods but known to friends, plants a new shrine with no idol in it. Beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: Freya and the Salt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. Years later, Coral guides travelers past a roadside shrine where strangers leave salt and small songs; the child — named Freya by the fire — runs ahead on the pass. Prayers go up unanswered and that is fine; the answering happens at dinner tables now. Final beat: belonging was never above — it was beside.
